pr_comments: As a note... There's a lot happening here. Does it make sense to break this up? I know the pieces won't work on their own, but it feels a little simpler?

> As a note... There's a lot happening here. Does it make sense to break this up? I know the pieces won't work on their own, but it feels a little simpler?

We currently have a couple of commits that are out of order, but we are squashing them as we progress with the port; the end PR is going to be really clean! :rocket: We are aiming for one commit per library.

Having a single PR that we can merge with rebase is going to ensure we can easily make use of git bisect to track down possible regressions that we didn't catch with the current tests

> We are aiming for one commit per library

I think you could reasonably do one PR per library.

> > We are aiming for one commit per library
> 
> I think you could reasonably do one PR per library.

The goal is to have a single PR with clean history that can be reviewed and merged all at once without risking to have foreign commits from other PRs in the middle. Committing parts that are not fully working or are incomplete/out of order will cause issues down the line when looking at the branch history or when bisecting.

Compared to freezing master and creating one consecutive PR at a time for each library, using a single PR that we merge with rebase is going to provide more context when reviewing the changes, cause less friction when the port is merged and also keep all commits correct and working.

just curious, would it be possible to review and merge in the LIEF library at #7160 and then include LIEF in this PR?
I think LIEF should support Silicon (it has releases for arm for macos)
Or will i need to add silicon support to my PR if this gets merged before the LIEF PR?
I dont have a silicon system to do any testing.

# Guide for PR reviewers

This PR is intimidatingly large, but it's not as large as the list of changed files would seem to imply.

* You can skim or ignore all of the `libraries/cmake/source/*/generated/*` files, which are all "generated automatically". This means these files have been pre-generated to create certain configuration-time artifacts that the third-party library dependencies need to build. This is not a change to how we're doing things, it just reflects that many of the libraries have been updated to newer versions and given support for Apple Silicon.
* You can skim or skip all of the submodules that are updated, and the `.cmake` scripts used to "find" these submodules. We have updated the versions of many libraries, this is just part of that change.
* There are a couple of dozen README files in `libraries/cmake/source/*`: this is just documentation for osquery maintainers, on how to integrate the many vendored dependencies with the osquery-toolchain. Now with comments for Apple Silicon. These are tips for the maintenance of the CMake build, and are consistent with the CMakeLists files. This is explained in the top-level `libraries/cmake/README.md`.
* We've been able to retire many `.patch` files: Retired some of our inter-release Thrift patches; retired a Boost patch. Retired a googletest patch. Also a yara patch.
* There are changes to about three dozen CMakeLists files. Note that we removed `lldpd` and `smartmontools` for M1 and recommend deprecation more generally later. Otherwise, we've made small improvements to passing the architecture to the various build files. AWS-SDK is huge and so there are many changes in that one, reflecting the changes in that dependency. Similar for Boost. These reflect the upstream changes.
* Small changes to `.h` files in libraries. You can see that many of these are the same change, and can be reviewed quickly. Others are updates to support building on Apple Silicon and/or the osquery-toolchain. Please ask here for rationale behind anything specific.
* Tests: a few tests needed to be fixed in order to pass on Apple Silicon / M1 machines.
* CI: lastly, we have the changes to the CI to support Apple Silicon builds, stitching a Universal Binary, signing and packaging.

Basically any open PR will have to be rebased after this one is merged, but I think we should handle that separately. Here we're adding cross-compilation, so the CI will provide feedback whether the PR will build in Apple Silicon. Developers won't need M1 to contribute, but, every new dependency being proposed will have to build for Apple Silicon. Hopefully the added READMEs will help.

Just to confirm, this means per-architecture and not Universal(2) builds, yes? (I like small binary sizes and don't mind the logistics overhead, but many places prefer the simplicity of one pkg that works for 'all'.)

> Just to confirm, this means per-architecture and not Universal(2) builds, yes? (I like small binary sizes and don't mind the logistics overhead, but many places prefer the simplicity of one pkg that works for 'all'.)

We might have to offer packages in x86, M1, and Universal if size ends up being an issue. If size weren't an issue, everyone would probably want Universal.

This PR is now ready to review.
Note that there are a couple of checks (build_macos on 10.15) which are still set as Required by Github, but they do not exist in this PR anymore.
Since they are still used for versions of code that are precedent to this PR, I suggest to disable them only in the moment we want to merge this PR.

issue_context.title: Update bzip2 to build natively on Apple Silicon
issue_context.body:
Background:

Building osquery natively on Apple silicon is primarily a matter of building all of its third-party dependencies (and consequently all of their dependencies) natively on Apple silicon, using the osquery toolchain and CMake-based build.

`bzip2` is used in `Boost` and `libarchive` dependencies.
